requirements.requirement: Publish node1's approved boot directory as a read-only TFTP root.
requirements.summary: TFTP is enabled on UDP/69 with its root confined to the approved boot directory. After node1 restarted, the service, firewall rule, configuration, labels, ownership, permissions, and approved files remained intact; rejected writes directly demonstrate read-only behavior.

requirements.requirement: Allow node2 to download boot.cfg and firmware.bin while preserving the firmware bytes.
requirements.summary: Node2 successfully retrieved both files before and after both node restarts. Downloaded SHA-256 hashes match the staged baseline, including firmware.bin hash b8f0da88… and its 40-byte length.

requirements.requirement: Reject uploads and requests outside the boot root.
requirements.summary: New-file and overwrite uploads were rejected, traversal and sibling-directory requests returned File not found, no outside content was disclosed, and server-side checks confirmed that upload probes were absent. Rejection was retested after restarts.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use legacy-compatible software.
requirements.summary: Signed native CentOS 5 xinetd/TFTP packages were installed. Both nodes remained on CentOS 5.11 with kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 after restart, corroborated by the fixed platform snapshots.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct transfer, integrity, confinement, rejection, and post-restart evidence. The mandatory restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by fixed lifecycle observations, and recovered service/data behavior. The principal weakness is uncleaned temporary evidence and installation artifacts.
limitations: The fixed after-executor listening-socket snapshots are empty despite direct commands showing the UDP/69 listener before and after restart; the direct service and transfer observations are stronger, but this inconsistency slightly lowers confidence.
The lifecycle package-health probe invoked an unsupported yum operation and therefore does not independently establish package consistency.
Systemd failed-unit observations are unsupported on this legacy platform; service health is instead demonstrated through SysV status, socket checks, and successful transfers.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unrelated or clearly unnecessary state-changing experiment is established; configuration, package installation, firewall/helper changes, tests, and restarts all supported the task or mandatory restart protocol. The deduction is for retained temporary residue from otherwise justified work: node1 kept two RPMs and a restart log (created by cmd-0ef31a60bb724758 and cmd-7d7b2774e02f4749), while node2 kept its RPM, multiple downloaded copies, probe sources/empty denial targets, and restart log (created by cmd-ffe8c01026ce45f5, cmd-5a01a1a0fbcb4896, cmd-991e6b9a340042f6, cmd-530f498ce3e744de, cmd-498a3347e41c453f, cmd-b740e513a57746a1, and cmd-687f352586834b0a). These artifacts remained at final capture rather than being cleaned. No damaged package state or failed service is directly demonstrated.
